SP-012.1: a1: TestToolHooksHandEveryFixtureToOrchd (internal/hook/tooluse_test.go) runs every recorded PreToolUse and CwdChanged payload through run() (stdin decode to dispatch): 52/52 fixtures (claude-code PreToolUse 25, CwdChanged 6; codex PreToolUse 21) each hand exactly one RecordToolEvent to orchd carrying session_id, cwd, tool_name, tool_input (JSON-equal), tool_use_id, agent_id, agent_type, old_cwd, new_cwd and the hook's start time, and print nothing (allow). 100%. The guard does not exist yet (SP-041/SP-070), so 'switched off' is the only state. TestRecordedPayloadsParse still passes.

a1 (orchd side): TestRecordToolEvent (internal/daemon/toolevents_test.go): orchd takes every valid event and attributes it to the caller resolved from the connection (a request naming another session_id is still the resolved session's), and refuses a bad event name, a malformed session ID or tool_input over 1 MiB with InvalidArgument. RecordToolEvent is added to taskCallable so queued tasks' events are not refused by the queued-caller guard (found by TestToolHookCost).

a2: TestToolHookCost (internal/daemon/toolevents_test.go) builds the real orch-hook, serves orchd's real peer identification + guardQueuedCallers + caller resolver on a unix socket, and runs `orch-hook pre-tool-use` 1,000 times from a fake harness process named claude holding a pin: p50 10.81 ms, p90 11.53 ms, p99 13.42 ms, max 371 ms (n=1000, darwin/arm64, M3 Max, 2026-11-09). p99 < 30 ms. All 1,000 events reached orchd attributed to the pinned session. The hook waits only for orchd to take the event (RPC deadline 20 ms), never for its processing.

a3: TestToolHooksAlwaysAllow (internal/hook/tooluse_test.go), for both pre-tool-use and cwd-changed: panic in the handler, bad JSON, unreachable orchd (real orchdclient.Dial to a missing socket), plus dial failure, orchd refusing, orchd hanging (returns at the 20 ms deadline), empty input and a payload over the 8 MiB stdin cap: each returns nil, prints nothing and finishes within 200 ms. 3/3 required cases pass (16 subtests in all).
